nearest_prior_work: Van Assche (2001), equations (24)-(26), gives the associated little-q-Legendre Pade coefficient Q_n(p^n) and the cyclotomic clearing d_n whose combination is the local C_n object.
Olive (1965) is a historical record-level lead for the q-Lucas root-of-unity decomposition used in the block split; the article text was not acquired or read, so no article-text support is asserted.
Wei-Gong-Wang (2012) exemplifies the established derivative-operator method that converts Chu-Vandermonde convolution into harmonic-number identities.

Guo-Zeng (2014), Section 4, equations (4.1)-(4.3), is nearby work on little-q-Legendre expansions and cyclotomic congruences using q-Chu-Vandermonde, but it does not study Van Assche's associated Pade coefficient or its resultants.
classification.attribution: Credit Van Assche for the little-q-Legendre Pade construction, explicit associated coefficient, and cyclotomic clearing; retain Olive only as an unresolved record-level lead for q-Lucas because the article text was not acquired or read; and credit the classical differentiated Chu-Vandermonde literature for the harmonic-collapse mechanism. Credit the local work only for the exact all-index synthesis for C_n and the n=15 certificate, with no priority claim and pending specialist confirmation.
classification.mathematical_interest: The factorization exposes a hidden quotient-remainder law in a concrete q-Pade coefficient and converts an otherwise intractable global resultant into exact local norms. The first crossing then turns a vague failure of estimates into a theorem that a natural global-height strategy is false.
classification.reusable_scope: The proof pattern may transfer to q-Pade families with a cyclotomic clearing envelope, q-Lucas block decomposition, and a moment tail reducible to differentiated hypergeometric summation. The negative lesson is broader: absolute full-resultant height can grossly overstate the prime powers selected by a specialized content or gcd.
classification.why_it_matters: The honest public story has two distinct contributions. The all-index formula is a source-backed, apparently unrecorded candidate identity built from standard ingredients; the n=15 corollary is a rigorous scoped no-go result that retires one proof route while leaving specialization-selective gcd control open. Neither is an Erdos-1049 solution or a field-level novelty claim.
